raw_response:
I am 63 years old and have been farming these 10 mu in Quzhou County since I was a teenager. I only finished primary school, so I do not read those extension pamphlets much — I learn by watching what happens on my own land and by talking to my neighbors. Every year I grow winter wheat followed by summer maize on all 10 mu. That is the system my father used, and it has never let me down. Wheat gives me grain I can sell easily, and maize gives me a second harvest from the same piece of ground. I thought about planting 2 mu of cotton instead, but at my age bending down to pick cotton is hard on my back, and wheat-maize is safer — the grain buyers always come to the village.

It is now spring, so my wheat went into the ground last October. I rotary-tilled before planting and sowed an improved variety, jimai22, using seed I bought from the supply shop. For fertilizer I spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and when the wheat greens up in spring I will topdress another 50 jin of urea at jointing. That works out to roughly 22 kg of nitrogen per mu. I do not buy much straight phosphorus or potassium — the compound fertilizer has a little bit, maybe 4 kg of phosphorus and 3 kg of potassium per mu, and the soil here is decent enough. I will irrigate four times: the winter irrigation, green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Water costs money, but four times is what my neighbors do and I do not want to risk drought. I spray pesticides about four times for wheat — herbicide once and insecticide two or three times when I see aphids.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I have less than a week to get the maize in. There is no time for ploughing, so I plant no-tillage. I use hybrid seed, denghai605, one small package per mu. I put down about 80 jin of compound fertilizer at planting — roughly 12 kg of nitrogen per mu — and hope the leftover fertility from the wheat helps too. I irrigate the maize twice, usually at the big-flare stage and grain filling, and spray pesticides three times. If the weather is normal I expect about 480 kg per mu from the wheat and 520 kg per mu from the maize. I know I could maybe save a little on fertilizer, but I would rather waste a few yuan than risk a bad harvest — my son is working in the city and I need to cover my own medical costs.
